title: Grateful Dead Live at Cameron Indoor Stadium, Duke U on 1973-12-08
lineage: CD -> Adobe Audition v3 -> Samplitude Professional v10.22 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD

ai_review.summary: High‑energy ’73 show with a monster Weather Report Suite, tight China > Rider jam and an otherworldly Other One, captured on a generally good soundboard recording despite occasional mix drops.
ai_review.review: Fans rave about the soaring Weather Report Suite, the razor‑tight China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider transition, and a wildly inventive Other One that borders on space. The soundboard source is mostly clear and lively, though a few listeners note a brief drop‑out of Johnny B’s vocals and a thin drum mix early in the first set.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating ≈4.66 /5, with overwhelmingly positive comments on both performance and recording; only one mixed review noting mix issues.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally crisp and balanced soundboard capture; occasional drop‑out of Johnny B’s vocal line, thin drum presence on the first set, a cut at ~6:06 in China Cat Sunflower, and minor pitch/tempo quirks noted in alternate remasters.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: A marathon first set (16 songs) followed by a second set packed with deep improvisations; rare Wharf Rat → Stella sequencing and two late‑night Jerry ballads give the show an unusual arc, while the jam from Nobody's Fault into The Other One provides the centerpiece.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His vocals are described as extra sweet and soulful; leads the Weather Report Suite with climatic guitar lines, delivers tight playing on China > Rider, and drives a heavy‑dark jam on The Other One while also providing two tender ballads late in the set.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass work gets special shout‑outs – a “Phil splurge” on the second solo of Rider and generally solid, funk‑filled underpinning throughout; noted as ‘priceless Phil’ by one reviewer.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bobby McGee highlighted as a standout performance; early mix emphasizes his guitar (some reviewers note drums are buried), and his vocal contribution is praised.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s playing shines on They Love Each Other and the Dragnet interlude; described as a “showpiece” with moments of brilliance, especially during the Rider solo.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s drumming is mostly well‑balanced but suffers from a thin mix in the first set according to one reviewer; otherwise provides solid drive for the high‑energy jams.
